Akhambhai ... on 12 September, 2024
 
 C/Fa/3144/2024 Ord

In The High Court Of Gujarat At Ahmedabad
 R/First Appeal No. 3144 of 2024
 With
 Civil Application (For Interim Relief) No. 1 of 2024
 In R/First Appeal No. 3144 of 2024
 ==========================================================
 Gujarat State Road Transport Corporation
 Versus
 Shardaben Wd/O Abajibhai Akhambhai Garasiya & Ors.

 Mr Hs Munshaw(495) for the Appellant(s) No. 1

The present First Appeal, under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, is preferred by the appellant-GSRTC, being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the judgment and award dated 12.7.2024 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, (Main) Panchmahals at Godhra in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.295 of 2021 by which the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs15,46,786/-
with 9% per annum interest to the claimant/s, holding opponents liable jointly and severally.

sentences.text:
2. Brief facts of the case are as under:
2.1 The claimants filed the claim petition stating that on NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3144/2024 ORDER DATED: 12/09/2024 undefined 17.7.2021, the deceased Abajibhai Akhambhai Garasiya was riding on Motorcycle No.GJ.20.AM.9730 as a pillion rider and the same was driven by Gamanbhai with moderate slow speed; at about 17.30 hours, they were passing through village Dhandhela, Ta.Fatehpura, the Gujarat State Road Transport ... vs Shardaben Wd/O Abajibhai Akhambhai ...

on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72152442/
1 opponent no.1 i.e. driver of ST bus no.GJ.18Z.7018 came driving his vehicle in rash and negligent manner and due to excessive speed, he lost control over the vehicle and dashed with the said motorcycle, due to which the accident occurred and the deceased succumbed to the injuries.
Therefore, the claim petition was filed by the claimants for compensation.
2.2 Notices were served to the opponents.
Opponent No.2- GSRTc filed the written statement denying the contents of the claim petition.
The Tribunal has framed the issues.
The oral as well as documentary evidence were led by the rival parties before the Tribunal.
After considering the documentary as well as oral evidence and submissions made at the bar, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition by awarding compensation as noted above.

2.3 Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal,
the present appeal is preferred by the appellant-GSRTC.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3144/2024 ORDER DATED: 12/09/2024 undefined 3.

Learned advocate for the appellant-insurance company has assailed the impugned judgment and award on the ground of negligence and quantum, more particularly, that looking to the manner in which the accident occurred, the driver of the motorcycle should have been held solely negligent for the accident or atleast contributory negligence should have been apportioned between both the vehicles, however, the learned Tribunal has erred in holding the ST bus driver solely negligent for the accident.

Further, though no arguments are advanced on the point of quantum, the said ground is raised in the memo of appeal to the effect that the age of the deceased was wrongly considered, the multiplier was wrongly applied and the income was wrongly considered by the learned Tribunal.

He,
therefore, submitted to admit this appeal on both these counts.
4. I have considered the submissions made at the bar and also gone through the material produced on record, including the impugned judgment and award.

5. As regards the first contention of apportionment of negligence between the two vehicles, it is clear from the manner in which the accident occurred, as stated in the FIR NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3144/2024 ORDER DATED: 12/09/2024 undefined and panchanama, that the accident occurred when the motorcycle was trying to overtake the ST bus.

The learned Tribunal has discussed the issue of negligence in paragraph no.9 by observing that the say of the claimant in the claim petition and the deposition is supported by the documentary evidence viz. complaint, panchanama,
inquest panchanama and P.M.Note; further, though the driver of the ST bus has deposed that the rider of motorcycle tried to over take the bus and it slipped but the bus did not dash with the motorcycle, but during the cross-examination, he admitted that the complaint of alleged incident was lodged against him and the chargesheet was also filed against him after investigation, however,
from the FIR and panchanama, it reveals that the ST bus has dashed with the motorcycle while overtaking and therefore, the learned Tribunal has concluded that there is ample evidence to prove negligence on the part of the driver of the ST bus and thus held the driver of ST bus negligent to the Gujarat State Road Transport ... vs Shardaben Wd/O Abajibhai Akhambhai ... on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72152442/
2 extent of 100% for the accident, which is just and proper and not required to be interfered with.
6.

sentences.text:
A reference to the recent judgment in the case of Prem Lal Anand & Ors. V/s Narendra Kumar &
Ors. reported in Scale 2024(9) Scale 406, wherein it is held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in paragraph no.13 as under:
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3144/2024 ORDER DATED: 12/09/2024 undefined "13.

entities.text:
Prem Lal Anand & Ors. V/s Narendra Kumar &
Ors. reported in Scale 2024(9) Scale 406
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the attending facts and circumstances, merely because a person was attempting to overtake a vehicle, cannot be said to be an act of rashness or negligence with nothing to the contrary suggested from the record.
Further, it is the claimant-appellant(s) who lost a member of their family.
Not only was the claimant-appellant, Prem Lal Anand doing an act which is an everyday occurrence on the road that is overtaking a vehicle, but resultantly suffered extensive injuries himself.
That apart, it has also been proved that the offending vehicle was driven rashly and negligently.
These two factors taken together lead us to the conclusion that the findings of contributory negligence against the appellant No.1 was erroneous and justified.
Consequently, the compensation awarded on this count has to be revised."
In view of the above ratio and the evidence of FIR and panchanama, the ST bus is to be held solely negligent for the accident, which is properly done by the learned Tribunal.
7. On the point of quantum, though grounds are raised in the appeal, no arguments are advanced by learned advocate for the appellant-GSRTC.

From the discussion made on the point of quantum in the impugned judgment, in paragraphs 10 to 19, the learned Tribunal has discussed each and every NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3144/2024 ORDER DATED: 12/09/2024 undefined aspect relevant for arriving at just and proper compensation by considering the evidence led before it and the ratio laid down in various judgments of the Hon'ble Apex Court, which is just and proper and is not required to be interfered with in this appeal.
8.
In view of the above, this appeal is required to be dismissed at the admission stage itself and therefore, the following order is passed.
9. In view of above, the following order is passed.
9.1 The present appeal is dismissed with no order as to costs.
Civil application also stands dismissed accordingly.

9.2 The amount lying with the Tribunal and/or in the FDR, if any, shall be disbursed to the claimant, along with accrued interest thereon if any, by account payee cheque, after proper verification and after following due procedure,
within a period of six weeks from today.
9.3 Record and proceedings be sent back to the concerned Tribunal, forthwith.
